row.title: Parity conjecture for random Cayley graphs of ${\rm PGL}_2(p)$
row.statement:
Let $G={\rm PGL}_2(p)$, with $p$ varying over primes, and consider random $4$-regular Cayley graphs over $G$. **Parity conjecture.** The girth of such graphs is almost surely even.

This conjecture is based on the paper's computer experiments for random $4$-regular Cayley graphs of ${\rm PGL}_2(p)$; no proof or resolution is supplied.
row.source_name: Alex Gamburd, Shlomo Hoory, Mehrdad Shahshahani, Aner Shalev and Balint Virag, “On the girth of random Cayley graphs”, arXiv:0707.1833 (2007).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0707.1833

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2007). “On the other hand in it was proved that the elements with algebraic number entries are diophantine and the following conjecture was made:”

row.title: Non-wedge homotopy conjecture for theta complexes of cube hypergraphs
row.statement:
Let $\operatorname{Cube}(n,k)$ be the hypergraph whose vertices are the vertices of an $n$-cube and whose hyperedges come from the $k$-dimensional faces of the $n$-cube, and let $\Theta(\operatorname{Cube}(n,k))$ be its theta complex. A wedge of same-dimensional spheres means a wedge in which all sphere summands have one common dimension. **Non-wedge homotopy conjecture.** For $0<k<n-2$ and $n$ sufficiently large,

$$
\Theta(\operatorname{Cube}(n,k))
$$

is not homotopy equivalent to a wedge of same-dimensional spheres. The conjecture is motivated by the computed examples and by the observation that the nontrivial homology groups span an increasing range of dimensions as $n$ increases; it is proposed as potentially useful for distinguishing $2$-SAT from $k$-SAT for $k\geq 3$.
row.source_name: James Conant and Oliver Thistlethwaite, “Boolean formulae, hypergraphs and combinatorial topology”, arXiv:0808.0739 (2010).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.0739

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2008).

row.title: Average-time complexity conjecture for perfect sorting by reversals
row.statement:
Let $n$ be the size of a random permutation, and let $T_{n,p}$ denote the number of strong interval trees with $n$ leaves and $p$ prime vertices. Define

$$
p_n=\frac{\sum_p 2^p T_{n,p}}{T_n},
$$

where $T_n$ is the total number of such trees with $n$ leaves. **Average-time complexity conjecture.** The average-time complexity of the algorithm described in Berard et al. for computing a parsimonious perfect scenario is polynomial, bounded by

$$
\mathcal O(n\sqrt n).
$$

The preceding analysis shows that the algorithm runs in polynomial time with probability $1$ as $n\to\infty$, but this does not by itself establish a polynomial average running time. The conjecture is motivated by computed values of $p_n$ through $n=25$, which appeared bounded by a constant close to $2$; the claimed average-time bound remains the issue under consideration.
row.source_name: Mathilde Bouvel, Cedric Chauve, Marni Mishna and Dominique Rossin, “Average-case analysis of perfect sorting by reversals”, arXiv:0901.2847 (2009).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.2847

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2009).

row.title: Bethe permanent lifting bound conjecture
row.statement:
Let $\boldsymbol{\theta}$ be a non-negative $n\times n$ matrix. For $M\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$, let $\tilde{\Psi}_M$ be the set of degree-$M$ graph-covering permutations and let $\boldsymbol{\theta}^{\uparrow\tilde{{\bm{P}}}}$ denote the matrix lifted according to $\tilde{{\bm{P}}}$. Then $\operatorname{perm}(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{\uparrow\tilde{{\bm{P}}}})$ is defined for every $\tilde{{\bm{P}}}\in\tilde{\Psi}_M$. **Bethe permanent lifting bound conjecture.** For any $M\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$,

$$
\Big\langle \! \operatorname{perm}\left(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{\uparrow\tilde{{\bm{P}}}}\right)\!\Big\rangle_{\tilde{{\bm{P}}}\in\tilde{\Psi}_M}\leqslant\big(\operatorname{perm}(\boldsymbol{\theta})\big)^M.
$$

Possibly the stronger pointwise inequality

$$
\operatorname{perm}\left(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{\uparrow\tilde{{\bm{P}}}}\right)\leqslant\big(\operatorname{perm}(\boldsymbol{\theta})\big)^M
$$

holds for every $M\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ and every $\tilde{{\bm{P}}}\in\tilde{\Psi}_M$. The weaker form would imply the claimed upper bound on the Bethe permanent; the conjecture is verified for the all-one matrix and for the matrices studied through finite graph covers, but remains open in general.
row.source_name: Pascal O. Vontobel, “The Bethe Permanent of a Non-Negative Matrix”, arXiv:1107.4196 (2012).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.4196

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2011). “In this subsection we list conjectures and open problems w.r.t.\ upper bounds on $\perm(\matrtheta)$ based on $\permBethe(\matrtheta)$.”

row.title: The Möbius function formula conjecture for intervals $[M_m,\pi]$
row.statement:
Let $M_m=24\ldots(2m)13\ldots(2m-1)$, and let $\pi$ be a permutation in $\mathcal{P}_0^n\cup\mathcal{P}_1^n$. Define the statistics $\lambda$, $\sigma$, $j^a$, $j^b$, $\epsilon$, $s$, $s_\theta$, and $\widehat{C}$ as in the preceding construction. In particular,

$$
\widehat{C}_\beta^\alpha(k,s)=\begin{cases}\binom{\alpha-2k}{\beta},&0\leqslant k<\frac{s}{2},\\binom{\alpha-2(s-k)+1}{\beta},&\frac{s}{2}\leqslant k<s.\end{cases}
$$

**Möbius function formula conjecture.** If $\pi$ begins with $12$, ends with $(n-1)n$, or contains a triple adjacency, then

$$
\mu(M_m,\pi)=0.
$$

Otherwise,

$$
\begin{aligned}
|\mu(M_m,\pi)|={}&\binom{\lambda}{\sigma}-\sum_{\tau=0}^{|j^b|-1}\sum_{\gamma=0}^{\tau}\sum_{\omega=\tau-\gamma}^{j^b_\gamma+s_b(\tau+1,|j^b|-1)-1}\widehat{C}^{\lambda-\tau-2}_{\sigma-\tau-1}(\omega,s)\\
&+\sum_{\tau=0}^{|j^a|-1}\left[\sum_{\gamma=1}^{j^a_\tau+s_a(0,\tau-1)}\widehat{C}^{\lambda-|j^b|-\tau}_{\sigma-|j^b|-\tau}(\gamma,s+1)+\sum_{\omega=1}^{\epsilon}\widehat{C}^{\lambda-|j^b|-\tau}_{\sigma-|j^b|-\tau}(\omega+1,s+1)\right].
\end{aligned}
$$

Moreover, the sign of $\mu(M_m,\pi)$ is positive if and only if $n$ is even.

This conjectural formula gives an explicit Möbius value for a broad class of permutation-poset intervals. It was checked computationally for all pairs $(m,n)$ with $m<6$ and $n<12$; the general formula remains unproved in the supplied source.
row.source_name: Jason P Smith, “On the Möbius Function of Permutations With One Descent”, arXiv:1306.5926 (2014).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.5926

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2013).

row.title: The planar dual conjecture for Laplacian quadratic forms
row.statement:
Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be connected planar graphs. Suppose they have embeddings into the $2$-sphere such that the dual graphs with respect to these embeddings are isomorphic as multigraphs.

**Planar dual conjecture.** The quadratic forms over $\mathbb{Z}$ represented by the combinatorial Laplacians of $G_1$ and $G_2$ are equivalent.

This conjecture proposes that, for connected planar graphs, the isomorphism type of the embedded dual graph determines the integral equivalence class of the Laplacian quadratic form. The source motivates it by computer experiments; no resolution is supplied here.
row.source_name: An Huang, Shing-Tung Yau and Mei-Heng Yueh, “Graph invariants from ideas in physics and number theory”, arXiv:1409.5853 (2015).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.5853

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2014).

row.title: The level-rank duality Hilbert-series conjecture for SH$^c$ modules
row.statement:
Let $N$ and $M$ be the parameters of the level-rank duality, let $X$ be the partially ordered set defined by the relations in the source, and let $\mathcal{A}(X)$ be the set of all P-partitions over $X$. Write $x_i=\sum_{j=i}^{N}n_j$ and let $(a;q)_\infty=\prod_{k=0}^{\infty}(1-aq^k)$ denote the $q$-Pochhammer symbol. **The level-rank duality Hilbert-series conjecture.** The Hilbert series of the SH$^c$ module satisfies

$$
\sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal{A}(X)}q^{|\lambda|}=\frac{(q^{N+M};q^{N+M})^{N-1}_{\infty}\prod_{i<j}(q^{x_i-x_j};q^{N+M})_{\infty}\prod_{i>j}(q^{N+M+x_i-x_j};q^{N+M})_{\infty}}{(q;q)_{\infty}^{N}}.
$$

This conjecture extends the explicitly computed low-rank cases and predicts that the P-partition generating function agrees with the minimal-model character expression associated with level-rank duality. The general Jordan–Hölder set of the poset is not known, making the required P-partition count difficult; the status is therefore unresolved.
row.source_name: Masayuki Fukuda, Satoshi Nakamura, Yutaka Matsuo and Rui-Dong Zhu, “SH^c Realization of Minimal Model CFT: Triality, Poset and Burge Condition”, arXiv:1509.01000 (2015).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.01000

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2015).

row.title: The recurrence classification conjecture for uniform shifts on the binary tree
row.statement:
Let $\mathbb{T}_{2}$ be the binary tree, and let ${\mathbf a}$ be an $L$-periodic rotor sequence. Define $\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{rec}}^{\mathrm{conj}}$ to consist of all shifts of sequences of the form

$$
\overline{(0,i_{1},j_{1},0,i_{2},j_{2},\ldots,0,i_{N},j_{N})},
$$

where $\{i_{\ell},j_{\ell}\}=\{1,2\}$ for $1\leq \ell\leq N$. **The binary-tree uniform-shift recurrence conjecture.** The rotor walk in the uniform shift model corresponding to ${\mathbf a}$ is recurrent almost surely if and only if ${\mathbf a}\in\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{rec}}^{\mathrm{conj}}$. This conjecture was verified computationally for $L\leq 12$, but its general validity remains open.
row.source_name: Sebastian Mueller and Tal Orenshtein, “Infinite excursions of rotor walks on regular trees”, arXiv:1511.05896 (2017).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.05896

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2015).

row.title: The Tu–Deng conjecture on binary Hamming weights
row.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer and let $t\in\{1,\ldots,2^k-2\}$. Define

$$
S_{t,k}=\Bigl\{(a,b)\in\bigl\{0,\ldots,2^k-2\bigr\}^2:a+b\equiv t\bmod 2^k-1,\ w(a)+w(b)<k\Bigr\}
$$

and let $P_{t,k}=\lvert S_{t,k}\rvert/2^k$.

**Tu–Deng conjecture.** For every such $k$ and $t$, one has

$$
P_{t,k}\leq \frac12.
$$

Here $w(n)$ denotes the Hamming weight, or number of $1$s in the binary expansion of $n$. The conjecture concerns the distribution of binary Hamming weights under addition modulo $2^k-1$; it is known in various special cases and has been checked computationally for several ranges of $k$. The paper proves that the inequality holds for a proportion of $t$ tending to $1$ as $k\to\infty$, but the full uniform assertion remains open.
row.source_name: Lukas Spiegelhofer and Michael Wallner, “The Tu–Deng Conjecture holds almost surely”, arXiv:1707.07945 (2018).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.07945

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2017).

Here $w(n)$ denotes the Hamming weight, or number of $1$s in the binary expansion of $n$. The conjecture concerns the distribution of binary Hamming weights under addition modulo $2^k-1$; it is known in various special cases and has been checked computationally for several ranges of $k$. The paper proves that the inequality holds for a proportion of $t$ tending to $1$ as $k\to\infty$, but the full uniform assertion remains open.

row.title: Minimum-cost homologous circulation algorithm for embedded directed graphs
row.statement: Let $D$ be a directed graph cellularly embedded on a possibly non-orientable surface $\mathbb{S}$ of Euler genus $g$, let $c\colon A(D)\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ be a cost function, and let $y\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^{A(D)}$ be a circulation. A circulation in $D$ is **homologous** to $y$ when it represents the same homology class. **Minimum-cost homologous circulation problem.** A minimum $c$-cost circulation in $D$ homologous to $y$ can be computed using at most $g^{O(g)}n^{3/2}$ arithmetic operations, where $n$ is the number of nodes of $D$. The proposed algorithmic bound concerns the case of integer homology on possibly non-orientable surfaces and directed graphs, for which the authors explain that existing results do not clearly apply; the problem is therefore posed as open.
row.source_name: Michele Conforti, Samuel Fiorin, Tony Huynh, Gwenaël Joret and Stefan Weltge, “The stable set problem in graphs with bounded genus and bounded odd cycle packing number”, arXiv:1908.06300 (2019).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.06300

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2019). “We therefore propose the following as an open problem.”

row.title: The density limit conjecture for the binary Ulam set
row.statement:
Let $
\mathcal{W}_{2,n}$ denote the set of binary words of length $n$, and let $V_n=\mathcal{U}(\{0,1\})\cap\mathcal{W}_{2,n}$. The density of the binary Ulam set is measured by $|V_n|/|\mathcal{W}_{2,n}|=|V_n|/2^n$. **Density limit conjecture.** There exists some $0<r<1$ such that

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{|V_n|}{|\mathcal{W}_{2,n}|}=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{|V_n|}{2^n}=r.
$$

The claim formalizes the observed convergence of the computed densities of binary words in the Ulam set; the source gives no proof or resolution.
row.source_name: Tej Bade, Kelly Cui, Antoine Labelle and Deyuan Li, “Ulam Sets in New Settings”, arXiv:2008.02762 (2020).
row.references:

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

row.title: Wilf-class and palindromic-prefix enumeration conjecture for Hertzsprung patterns
row.statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}_k$ denote the set of Hertzsprung patterns of length $k$, and let $\Omega(\sigma,\sigma)$ be the autocorrelation polynomial of $\sigma\in\mathcal{S}_k$. For a palindrome $w\in\{0,1\}^k$, let $P(w)$ be the set of lengths of its palindromic prefixes. Define

$$
a_k=|\{\Omega(\sigma,\sigma):\sigma\in\mathcal{S}_k\}|,
$$

and let $b_k$ be the number of distinct sets $P(w)$ for palindromes $w\in\{0,1\}^k$. **Wilf-class and palindromic-prefix enumeration conjecture.** For $k\geq 3$, one has

$$
a_k=b_{k+1}.
$$

The equality is supported by the computed values through $k=15$, which agree with the OEIS sequence A304178 from $k\geq3$; a general proof is not supplied.
row.source_name: Anders Claesson, “From Hertzsprung's problem to pattern-rewriting systems”, arXiv:2012.15309 (2021).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.15309

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

row.title: The diffsequence growth conjecture for powers of two
row.statement:
Let $D=\{2^i\mid i\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\}$, and let $\Delta(D,k)$ denote the diffsequence parameter studied in the paper for the set $D$ and positive integer $k$. **Diffsequence growth conjecture.**
When $D=\{2^i\mid i\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\}$,

$$
\Delta(D,k)=2^{\Theta(\sqrt{k})}.
$$

The paper establishes a lower bound with exponent $\Theta(\sqrt{k})$ and an upper bound with exponent $\Theta(k)$, while computed values through $k=12$ closely match the lower bound. The conjecture asserts that the lower bound is asymptotically tight.

row.title: The strict lower-bound conjecture for binary subword entropy
row.statement:
Let $L_2$ denote the asymptotic binary subword-entropy constant, and let $\log_2$ be the logarithm to base $2$. **Strict lower-bound conjecture.**

$$
L_2 > \log_2(3/2).
$$

This conjecture is supported by exhaustive computations suggesting that the universal lower bound is not tight, although the available data are limited to small word lengths and the claim remains open.
row.source_name: Wenjie Fang, “Maximal number of subword occurrences in a word”, arXiv:2406.02971 (2025).

row.title: Positivity conjecture for Newton-polytope support coefficients
row.statement:
For $w\in S_n$, write

$$
\theta_w=1+\sum_u d_u\,p_u(w),
$$

where $\theta_w$ is the number of supports of $\mathfrak{S}_w(x)$ and $p_u(w)$ counts occurrences of the permutation pattern $u$ in $w$. The coefficients are computed recursively by

$$
d_u=\theta_u-1-\sum_{\sigma\in S_\ell\atop \ell<m}d_\sigma\,p_\sigma(u),
$$

with the same stability property $d_u=0$ when the final entry of $u\in S_m$ is $m$. **Support-coefficient positivity conjecture.** For any permutation $u$, $d_u\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. This is presented as an analogue of Gao's conjecture; no general resolution is given.
row.source_name: Peter L. Guo and Zhuowei Lin, “Schubert polynomials and patterns in permutations”, arXiv:2412.02932 (2024).
row.references:

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2024).

row.title: Tractability conjecture for graph Ramsey achievement games
row.statement: Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, let $A$ be the achievement graph, and let $E^r$ and $E^g$ be the precolored red and green edge sets. **Achievement-game tractability conjecture.** Graph Ramsey achievement games played on $(K_n,A,E^r,E^g)$ are tractable. This conjecture is motivated by evidence of tractable subcases, although the paper does not establish tractability in the full stated setting.

row.title: 2-EXPSPACE-completeness conjecture for Ramsey-number avoidance games
row.statement: Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, let $\mathrm{Ramsey}(n,n)$ be the symmetric binary Ramsey number, and let $K_{\mathrm{Ramsey}(n,n)}$ be the complete graph on that many vertices. **Explicit-Ramsey-number avoidance conjecture.** The graph Ramsey avoidance games played on $(K_{\mathrm{Ramsey}(n,n)},K_n,\{\},\{\})$ are $2$-${\bf EXPSPACE}$-complete. This conjecture is presented as a consequence of the preceding conjectures: computing explicit Ramsey numbers and manipulating graphs of their size suggests doubly exponential space requirements under succinct input representations.

row.title: Knutson's puzzle conjecture for two-step flag varieties
row.statement:
Let $F(a,b;N)$ be a two-step flag variety, and let $X_u$, $X_v$, and $X_w$ be Schubert varieties indexed by permutations $u,v,w\in S_N$. Write $J(u)$, $J(v)$, and $J(w)$ for their associated $012$-strings. A puzzle is a tiling by the six specified $012$-puzzle pieces, allowing rotations but not reflections.

**Knutson's conjecture.** The integral

$$
\int_{F(a,b;N)} [X_u]\cdot [X_v]\cdot [X_w]
$$

is equal to the number of puzzles whose north-west, north-east, and south boundary labels, read clockwise, are $J(u)$, $J(v)$, and $J(w)$, respectively.

This is a proposed combinatorial rule for Schubert structure constants on two-step flag varieties. It had been verified computationally for all such varieties with $N\leqslant 16$, while the broader conjecture for all partial flag varieties was disproved by counterexamples.

row.references:

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2003).

row.title: Polynomial-growth conjecture for Möbius values of the permutations $\pi_{n,k}$
row.statement:
For $k\le n$, let $\pi_{n,k}$ be the subpermutation of $\kappa_n$ induced by the values $n+1,n+3,\dots,n+2k-1,1,3n+1,2,3n+2,\dots,n,4n,n+2,n+4,\dots,n+2k$. In particular, $\pi_{n,1}=\pi_n$. **Polynomial-growth conjecture.** For every fixed $k\ge 1$, the absolute value of the Möbius function grows as

$$
|\mu(1,\pi_{n,k})|=\Theta(n^{k^2+6k}).
$$

This refines the authors' computed example $\pi_n=\pi_{n,1}$ and is supported by their intuition and preliminary results; the source gives no proof or resolution.
row.source_name: Vít Jelínek, Ida Kantor, Jan Kynčl and Martin Tancer, “On the growth of the Möbius function of permutations”, arXiv:1809.05774 (2019).
row.references:

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2018).

row.title: Asymptotic conjectures for the crossroads sequences $L_n$ and $M_n$
row.statement:
Let $L_n$ and $M_n$ be the two integer sequences studied in the paper, and let $C_n$ denote the $n$th Catalan number. The known values include $M_n>L_n$ for $9\leq n\leq14$.

**Conjectures for $L_n$ and $M_n$.** The following five propositions are conjectured:

$$
\forall n\in\mathbb{N},\ n\geq 9\Rightarrow M_n>L_n,
$$

$$
\lim_{n\to+\infty}\frac{M_n}{L_n}=+\infty,
$$

$$
\lim_{n\to+\infty}\frac{M_n}{C_n}=1,
$$

$$
\lim_{n\to+\infty}\frac{L_n}{C_n}=0,
$$

$$
\lim_{n\to+\infty}\frac{M_{n+1}}{M_n}=\lim_{n\to+\infty}\frac{L_{n+1}}{L_n}=4.
$$

The sequences $L_n$ and $M_n$ have only been computed for small values because the available algorithms have exponential complexity. These conjectures describe their eventual ordering, their asymptotic comparison with each other and with the Catalan numbers, and their limiting consecutive-term growth.
row.source_name: Julien Rouyer and Alain Ninet, “Two New Integer Sequences Related to Crossroads and Catalan Numbers”, arXiv:2311.07181 (2024).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.07181

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2023).
